Examples.Title: Delete a lab report session
Examples.Description: Soft-delete a session. It is marked deleted immediately; associated storage is cleaned up by a background process.
Examples.Setup: This example assumes `using Terra;` is in scope and `apiKey` contains the required credential.

Examples.Title: Retrieve a lab report session
Examples.Description: Retrieve a report's metadata, results, reference ranges, and status history. Immutable and cacheable — presigned file URLs and mutable per-destination delivery state live on the `/files` and `/deliveries` sub-resources.
Examples.Setup: This example assumes `using Terra;` is in scope and `apiKey` contains the required credential.

Examples.Title: List lab report sessions
Examples.Description: List lab report sessions for your account, with optional reference, upload, and inclusive date-range filters. Use the date filters to narrow large result sets.
Examples.Code:
using var client = new TerraClient(apiKey);
var response = await client.LabReports.LabReportsListAsync();
Examples.Setup: This example assumes `using Terra;` is in scope and `apiKey` contains the required credential.

Examples.Title: List delivery outcomes
Examples.Description: The per-destination delivery state for a report. Each opted-in destination is tracked independently, so one failure never hides delivery to the others (and is why a session can be `partially_sent`).
Examples.Setup: This example assumes `using Terra;` is in scope and `apiKey` contains the required credential.

Examples.Title: List input files
Examples.Description: The uploaded input files and report thumbnail, with freshly minted presigned download URLs. URLs expire; fetch again to mint new ones.
Examples.Setup: This example assumes `using Terra;` is in scope and `apiKey` contains the required credential.

Examples.Title: Upload a lab report
Examples.Description: Upload a single lab report file (PDF, PNG, JPEG, GIF, or WebP) as multipart form data. Returns an `upload_id`; a single upload may fan out to multiple sessions, so learn the `session_id`(s) from the webhook events or from `GET /lab-reports?upload_id=...`.
Examples.Code:
### Upload a lab report
# @name LabReports_Upload
POST {{host}}/lab-reports?reference_id=patient_456
Authorization: Bearer {{token}}
Content-Type: multipart/form-data
Accept: application/json, application/problem+json

# Description: The credential is not authorized for this operation.

Examples.Title: Create a workout template
Examples.Description: Stores a reusable workout template. Plan it onto a user's calendar with `POST /workouts/{workout_id}/plan`; the template itself carries no date and is not pushed to any provider until planned.
Examples.Code:
### Create a workout template
# @name Workouts_CreateWorkout
POST {{host}}/workouts
Authorization: Bearer {{token}}
Content-Type: application/json
Accept: application/json, application/problem+json

{
  "name": "string",
  "description": "string",
  "sport": "running",
  "environment": "indoor",
  "pool_length_meters": 0,
  "step_blocks": [
    {
      "completion_condition": {},
      "steps": []
    }
  ],
  "estimated_duration_seconds": 0,
  "estimated_distance_meters": 0,
  "estimated_calories": 0,
  "workout_id": "string"
}

Examples.Title: List planned workouts
Examples.Description: Returns the user's planned workouts, including workouts created on the provider side (is_external true) where the provider exposes them. External workouts carry their full body (title, description, planned metrics, structured steps) under `details`; they are fetched live from the provider and are not stored by Terra. Note that providers may limit how far ahead planned workouts are visible.
Examples.Code:
### List planned workouts
# @name Workouts_ListPlannedWorkouts
GET {{host}}/plannedWorkouts?user_id={{user_id}}&start_date={{start_date}}&end_date={{end_date}}
Authorization: Bearer {{token}}

Examples.Title: Plan a workout onto a user's calendar
Examples.Description: Schedules the workout template for a user on a given date and pushes it to the user's connected provider (or queues it for SDK delivery). Athlete metrics personalise zone-based targets for this plan only.
Examples.Code:
### Plan a workout onto a user's calendar
# @name Workouts_PlanWorkout
POST {{host}}/workouts/{{workout_id}}/plan?user_id={{user_id}}
Authorization: Bearer {{token}}
Content-Type: application/json
Accept: application/json, application/problem+json

{
  "planned_date": "2025-01-01",
  "ftp": 0,
  "max_heart_rate": 0,
  "threshold_heart_rate": 0,
  "threshold_speed": 0,
  "pool_length_meters": 0
}
